rule.description: A function signature repeatedly carries an ext value's metadata as separate bare scalars: one parameter of payload-size type (u32 or usize) for the ext payload length and one parameter of type-id type (i8) for the application type tag, instead of the cohesive (size, type) record the codebase already models as ExtMeta.

checks.description: Dylint lint 'ext_meta_data_clump' (library ext_meta_clump, run over the workspace library targets via cargo-dylint): flag every non-closure function whose declared parameter list contains both at least one payload-size scalar parameter (u32 or usize) and at least one type-id scalar parameter (i8), which is the signature shape of the ext metadata pair being threaded as separate bare parameters. A workspace crate carrying two or more such signatures means the pair is really traveling through that crate's internals as an unbundled clump rather than as an intentional single public primitive.
checks.detected_relation: ext payload-size parameter + ext type-id parameter declared separately in the same function signature
checks.why_this_is_the_smell: The payload size and the application type id form one conceptual ext metadata record (already modeled by rmp::decode::ExtMeta); declaring them as separate parameters in signature after signature forces every caller to repeat both values in lockstep, provides no shared type documenting that the two belong together, and lets the pair drift in order or meaning between call sites.

matches.evidence: pub fn write_ext_meta<W: RmpWrite>(wr: &mut W, len: u32, ty: i8) declares the ext metadata pair as two bare parameters; this is the long-standing public primitive the internal helpers imitate (pinned public API, reported as the anchor match of the cluster).
pub(super) fn write_ext_header<W: RmpWrite>(wr: &mut W, len: u32, ty: i8) forwards the same ext metadata pair as separate bare parameters while emitting the marker, size and type id.

fn write_ext_value<W: Write>(wr: &mut W, ty: i8, len: u32, data: &[u8]) carries the ext metadata pair as separate bare scalars alongside the payload it describes; the len parameter is even derivable from data.

fn write_ext_value_ref<W: Write>(wr: &mut W, len: u32, ty: i8, data: &[u8]) is the borrowed-value twin of write_ext_value, repeating the same separate (size, type) parameters with a different parameter order.
fn write_ext_field_bytes<W: Write>(wr: &mut W, len: u32, tag: i8, data: &[u8]) threads the pair under different names (len/tag) through the serde ext-field serialization path.
The ExtDeserializer constructor takes (len: u32, ty: i8) as separate fields, eagerly storing the pair read from the wire instead of one bundled ext metadata record.

excluded.reason: The struct ExtMeta { typeid: i8, size: u32 } is the bundled record the repair should use, not an offender; the rule inspects function signatures only, and its field pair is the cohesion the smell erodes.
Decode-side readers already return the bundled ExtMeta record, so they do not thread the pair as separate parameters.
Fixed-size ext readers take only the reader and return the type id with the fixed payload, so they never carry the full pair through a signature.

Functions taking only the payload size (len: usize, no i8 parameter) never carry the full pair through a signature; padding a signature with an unused type id to trigger the rule would be artificial, and the rule does not require it.
The borrowed-value twin of the owned decoder takes only the payload size (len: usize, no i8 parameter), so it matches the rule's signature shape nowhere.

The enum variants Ext(i8, Vec<u8>) and Ext(i8, &[u8]) carry the type id next to the payload rather than next to a payload-size scalar, and they are data definitions, not the repeated signature shape this rule measures.

excluded.symbol: impl Serialize for Value -- Self::Ext arm
excluded.reason: The serde-model bridge wraps the pair as a (ty, Bytes) newtype value and hands it to serde; no separate payload-size scalar is threaded through a signature.
The decode side of the ext bridge takes (tag, data) with the payload carried by the byte buffer itself, so no separate payload-size scalar participates in the signature-shape relation.
